text: The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah—that was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon—
the word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem:

From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until this very day—twenty-three years now—the word of the LORD has come to me, and I have spoken to you again and again, but you would not listen.
The LORD sent you all his servants the prophets, again and again, but you would not listen; you would not turn your ear to hear.
They said: Turn back, each of you, from your evil way and from your wicked deeds, and live on the land the LORD gave to you and to your fathers forever and ever.
Do not follow other gods to serve them and bow down to them. Do not provoke me to anger with the work of your hands, and I will do you no harm.
But you would not listen to me, declares the LORD; instead you provoked me to anger with the work of your hands, to your own harm.
Therefore this is what the LORD of hosts says: Because you have not listened to my words,

I am sending for all the tribes of the north, declares the LORD, and for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will bring them against this land and its inhabitants and against all these surrounding nations. I will devote them to destruction and make them an object of horror and scorn, an everlasting ruin.
I will banish from them the sound of joy and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
This whole land will become a ruin and a wasteland, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

versions.text: This whole land will become a desolate waste, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon seventy years.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has two distinct nouns (חָרְבָּה, ruin; שַׁמָּה, desolation/horror). Rendering them as the single phrase "a desolate waste" flattens the pairing; two coordinated nouns also read with a stronger rhythm aloud and match the similar pairing rendered in verses 9 and 18.

text: But when the seventy years are complete, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation for their guilt, declares the LORD, and the land of the Chaldeans too, and I will make it a desolation forever.

versions.text: But when the seventy years are complete, I will call the king of Babylon and that nation to account for their guilt, declares the LORD, and the land of the Chaldeans as well, and I will make it a desolation forever.
versions.explanation: The clause "and the land of the Chaldeans as well" is stranded after the quotation formula, making the sentence hard to follow when read aloud. Placing the objects together before "declares the LORD" keeps the Hebrew sense of פקד על ("punish/visit upon") and reads more smoothly.

text: I will bring upon that land everything I have spoken against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
For they too will be enslaved by many nations and great kings, and I will repay them according to their deeds and the work of their hands.
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, said to me: Take this cup of the wine of wrath from my hand and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.
They will drink and stagger and go mad because of the sword I am sending among them.
So I took the cup from the LORD's hand and made all the nations to whom he sent me drink it:
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin and an object of horror, of scorn and cursing, as they are today;
Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials and all his people;
all the mixed peoples; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines—Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron, and what is left of Ashdod;
Edom, Moab and the Ammonites;
all the kings of Tyre and all the kings of Sidon; the kings of the coastlands across the sea;
Dedan, Tema, Buz and all who clip the hair at their temples;
all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed peoples who live in the desert;
all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam and all the kings of Media;
all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another—and all the kingdoms of the world that are on the face of the earth. And after them the king of Sheshach will drink too.

versions.text: all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another—and all the kingdoms on the face of the earth. And after them the king of Sheshach will drink too.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has a fuller expression, "all the kingdoms of the earth which are upon the face of the ground"; the current rendering collapses the two phrases into one. It would also help the reader to add a footnote at "Sheshach" explaining that this is a coded name for Babylon.

text: Then say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel, says: Drink, get drunk, vomit, and fall to rise no more, because of the sword I am sending among you.
And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, say to them: This is what the LORD of hosts says: You must drink it!

See, I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears my name, and will you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for I am summoning the sword against all who live on the earth, declares the LORD of hosts.

So prophesy all these words against them and say to them: The LORD roars from on high; from his holy dwelling he thunders. He roars mightily against his fold; like those who tread the grapes he shouts against all who live on the earth.
The uproar reaches the ends of the earth, for the LORD has a case against the nations; he brings judgment on all flesh and hands the wicked over to the sword, declares the LORD.
This is what the LORD of hosts says: Look! Disaster is spreading from nation to nation, and a mighty storm is rising from the ends of the earth.
On that day those slain by the LORD will lie from one end of the earth to the other. No one will mourn them; they will not be gathered or buried, but will lie like dung on the ground.
Wail, you shepherds, and cry out! Roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock! For the days of your slaughter have come; you will be scattered and fall like a choice vessel.

versions.text: Wail, you shepherds, and cry out! Roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock! For the time of your slaughter has come; you will be scattered and fall like a fine vessel shattered.
versions.explanation: 'Shattered' is not in the Hebrew (כִּכְלִי חֶמְדָּה = 'like a choice/precious vessel'); the image is of falling, and the added participle is an unnecessary expansion. Also 'the time of your slaughter' flattens the plural 'your days ... are full'.

text: There will be no refuge for the shepherds, no escape for the leaders of the flock.
Hear the cry of the shepherds, the wailing of the leaders of the flock, for the LORD is destroying their pasture.
The peaceful meadows are silenced before the burning anger of the LORD.
Like a lion he has left his lair, for their land has become a desolation because of the oppressor's fierce anger, because of the burning anger of the LORD.

versions.text: Like a lion he has left his lair, for their land has become a desolation before his fierce oppression, before his burning anger.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew הַיּוֹנָה is a participle meaning 'the oppressor' (or 'the oppressing one'), so the phrase is 'the fierce anger of the oppressor,' not 'his fierce oppression.' Rendering it as God's 'oppression' both mistranslates the noun and attributes oppression to the LORD, which is a theological distortion. A footnote could note the textual difficulty of הַיּוֹנָה.
